L61: ## Current Clinical Trials
L62: 
L63: 【45†Image: Very Cute Cats】
L64: UC Davis Veterinary Medicine conducts 30-50 research studies at any given time, including basic science, translational, and clinical trial research — all with the goal of bringing new, effective and safe treatments to our veterinary patients more quickly. Use 【22†Study Pages†studypages.com】 to browse and connect with active recruiting studies at UC Davis Veterinary Medicine.
L65: Through 【22†Study Pages†studypages.com】, potential participants may find out more information about studies and contact study staff to see if their pet may be eligible.

L20: # Clinical Trials
L21: ## Providing compassionate care while advancing the field of veterinary medicine
L22: 
L23: Clinical trials are where patient care and innovation intersect. They allow us to offer our hospital clients unique treatment options for their pets while simultaneously making groundbreaking advancements in veterinary medicine. They are often conducted as part of the development of new medications, procedures, or therapies, and all animals participating in trials receive excellent clinical care.
L24: Clinical trials are conducted with approval from the Clinical Research Committee, the Hospital Board, and the University of Georgia Research Foundation. This is often the end-stage testing to determine the safety and degree of effectiveness for new drugs or treatments before FDA approval.
L25: 
L26: 【9†Search Clinical Trials】
L27: ### Frequently Asked Questions
L28: 
L29: What are the benefits of participating in a clinical trial?
L30: Participation in a clinical trial means that your animal can receive a treatment option for their illness/injury that might not be available through other avenues. These may include novel procedures or medications that are under study. Participants in clinical trials also contribute to the advancement of medical research, and may help to validate a new drug or approach that will become more widely available for other pets.
L31: Pets that are participants in clinical trials receive close monitoring and other standard of care observation just as other patients. Participants in clinical trials may receive medication or other treatments at a reduced cost.
L32: Are there risks involved in participating?
L33: All of our clinical trial participants receive excellent veterinary care just like all of our other hospital patients. However, they are designed to study novel procedures that may have unanticipated side-effects that would not be expected with the standard treatment options. In addition, the new treatment may not work for your pet, even if it benefits other patients in the clinical trial.
L34: Participants in clinical trials may require more frequent veterinary visits and tests compared to standard therapy, as all patients are closely monitored. All potential risks and benefits will be discussed with you in detail before enrolling in the clinical trial, and you may stop participation in the trial at any time if desired.
L35: To help ensure the safety of participants, all clinical trials performed at the Veterinary Teaching Hospital must be approved by the Clinical Research Committee, the Hospital Board, and the University of Georgia Research Foundation.
L36: Am I compensated for participating in a clinical trial?
L37: 
L38: Although some clinical trials cover most or all of the costs to the pet owner, others only partially cover the cost of diagnostic tests and/or treatments. Please refer to each clinical trial listing for more information.
L39: 
L40: How can I find out if my pet qualifies for a study?
L41: 
L42: Each clinical trial has specific criteria that patients must meet to be candidates for inclusion. Please refer to specific clinical trial listings for more information
L43: What are my responsibilities if my pet is enrolled in a clinical trial?
L44: This also varies by trial, and you should be sure that you can meet the requirements before signing the Owner Informed Consent. If you have any questions about the study, please ask your veterinarian or study staff for clarification. Some studies will require diagnostic tests to be performed at your veterinarian at specific intervals, or may require you to keep track of your pet’s behavior at home.
L45: In addition, please note the study schedule if your pet will be required to have recheck examinations performed with your vet or at UGA. In addition, if the health of your pet changes, or you are no longer willing to participate in the study, please notify the principal investigator.
L46: Who should I contact if I have additional questions?
L47: 
L48: To learn more about our clinical trials, please contact our Clinical Research Coordinator.
